subject: Request: executive waiver for ramp & early-unwind opt-out — Stellar Health

Subject: Request: executive waiver for ramp & early-unwind opt-out — Stellar Health

Vivek,

Quick summary and ask: Stellar Health (procurement looping) is pushing for a non-standard ramp schedule and an early-unwind opt-out that would allow them to reduce committed capacity at 60 days with a partial credit. They are a high-priority enterprise (large payer customer) with clear expansion upside. Deal details attached (SOW_StellarHealth_v2.pdf, redlines).

Key asks for exec sign-off:
- Approve a 90-day staged ramp instead of our standard 30/60 ramp (monthly stair-step: 10% -> 40% -> 70% -> committed at 90d).
- Allow a limited early-unwind opt-out at day 60 with a capped credit equal to 25% of the remaining 6 months' committed fees (to be issued as one-time credit if they downsize).
- One-time 10% onboarding discount tied to the 12-month committed term.

Risks we flagged: increased short-term churn exposure, potential precedent for other enterprise deals. Mitigations proposed in attached ramp_schedule_table.csv and proposed contractual language in redlines_SH-4823.docx (see §4.2-4.4).

Timeline: They want response by EOD Wednesday so procurement can align with their board review next week.

Can you sign off or suggest approvals/conditions? If you prefer, we can present two options (tighter credit cap vs. no opt-out).

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Request: executive waiver for ramp & early-unwind opt-out — Stellar Health

Thanks for the summary, Marissa. A few clarifying Qs before I weigh in: 

1) How material is the 12-month ARR to our quarterly book if they exercise the opt-out at 60 days? Do we get any minimum fees for the first 60 days?
2) Why is Stellar proposing a 90-day commit to reach full capacity — is this operational readiness on their side or concerns around model costs?
3) Can Karthik confirm that the proposed credit is limited to non-recurring credits (i.e., one-off account credit) and that it cannot be used to offset future committed fees beyond the current term?

Preliminarily I am open to a limited waiver if: (a) the credit cap is firm and non-extendable; (b) we insert language to ensure this is a single exception and does not create a template; and (c) we get an additional revenue commitment (10% premium on committed months after month 3 if they remain).

If we move forward, I want the approval to include explicit guardrails: auto-fallback to hosted profile if usage patterns appear anomalous, and a hard sunset on the opt-out window.

Vivek

Subject: Re: Request: executive waiver for ramp & early-unwind opt-out — Stellar Health

Vivek/Marissa —

I reviewed the redlines and drafted recommended contract language to limit future precedent and protect Redwood's exposure. Main points: 

- Credit mechanics: "If Customer elects to downsize within the 60- to 90-day window, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 25% of the remaining, prepaid committed fees for the then-current term. Such credit is non-transferable, non-recurring, and may not be applied to any future renewal term." (This language ensures credit is one-time.)

- Ramp schedule: "Customer will adhere to the phased ramp schedule set forth in Schedule A: 10% month 1, 40% month 2, 70% month 3, full committed capacity month 4. Failure to reach the thresholds will trigger a review and potential temporary reversion to standard hosted profiles until performance stabilizes."

- Opt-out guardrail: "Opt-out right is conditioned on Customer providing 30 days' notice and paying the applicable early-unwind administration fee of $15,000 to cover transition costs. The opt-out window closes at day 90 and may not be re-invoked in subsequent renewal years."

- Precedent clause: add explicit clause that this agreement is a one-off concession for deal SH-4823 and cannot be cited as precedent by other customers without prior written consent of Redwood's Executive Team.

I recommend we tighten the credit cap to 20% if possible and require the $15k admin fee; that materially reduces our risk. If Stellar pushes back, we can accept 25% but only with board-level approval on their side and an addendum that ties any extension to a premium rate.

—I can push these edits into the redline doc and circulate a final SOW for signature if you give the green light.

Karthik

Customer is asking for a written confirmation of executive approval before they route to procurement. If we can get sign-off (or conditional sign-off with the 20% cap), procurement will proceed to counter-signature by Friday.

Marissa
